text:
maria: heads-up — after the kernel-selector v2 rollout last night, we're seeing ~10-13% higher host CPU on streaming-heavy pods. flamegraph points at parse/tokenize hotspots, not GPU.
aj: saw alerts. KV cache miss rate jumped too? saw a spike in kvcache.miss on the same instances.
maria: yep, kvcache miss rate up ~20pp (4% -> 24%) for requests with small prefix tokens. suspect change in how we shard proto-unpack frames prevents early kvcache lookup.
kevin: is this grpc-only? or does http1 path show it too?
maria: both, but http1 hosts show bigger variance. http/1.1 keepalive chunking tends to amplify the extra work.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: kernel-selector v2 rolled to prod at 2026-02-21T03:12:10Z (release/ingress-optimizations).
ravi: uploaded a 30s pprof from an affected host: https://perf.redwood/internal/pprof/2765439998/pprof
ravi: quick flame: https://perf.redwood/internal/flame/2765439998
maria: paste of perf top (aggregated):
```
  samples pcnt  function
  4120   18.4% parse::tokenize
  2780   12.4% proto::unpack_frame
  2230   10.0% hostpreproc::prefetch_debounce
  1500    6.7% kvcache::lookup (miss path)
  1200    5.4% io::grpc::read_frame
```
aj: interesting the hostpreproc debounce shows up — that's new. v2 changed windowing heuristic for kernel selection, maybe it nudges preparse to do extra scanning.
kevin: i ran a microbench on staging (streaming 64B tokens, 500rps) — tokenization cost per req increased ~18% with v2. Full trace attached in staging logs.
maria: sample log fragment showing extra proto scans:
```
[ingress] parsing frame headers: frames=3 scan_bytes=2048 preparse_scan=1024
[ingress] early_kv_lookup=false shard_hint=7
```
aj: options for mitigation:
- revert kernel-selector v2 (fast, but loses some batching wins)
- patch proto-unpack to preserve early kvcache hinting (fixes root cause)
- reduce preparse debounce window (8ms -> 4ms) to avoid extra scans
- canary v2 with proto-unpack patch only on http2/gRPC
kevin: agree. revert buys time but we should also prepare a non-reverting patch that keeps batching heuristics but restores kvcache hint.
maria: i profiled the batching heuristics: when kernel-selector picks GPU+long-window, we see aggregation that changes token boundaries and prevents prefix caching. KV keys are sequence-prefix based, so re-batching breaks hit patterns.
ravi: i ran a quick experiment: toggling batching-window back to 6ms reduces kvcache miss to ~9% and host CPU delta to ~3%.
aj: actionable plan:
- @aj will create a canary that reverts the kernel selector change for 10% traffic for next 2 hours (to confirm delta)
- @kevin will open PR to restore early-kv-hint in proto-unpack and add unit test for prefix-preservation
- @ravi will collect pprof + flame for canary vs v2 and post before/after
- @maria will coordinate SLO oncall notification and pause any further rollout
sre-oncall: logging alert thresholds adjusted + added kvcache.miss rate graph to dashboard :eyes:
maria: also note: http1 path had larger penalty due to repeated small-writes causing extra parse churn. if we can coalesce microwrites on proxy we might get additional wins — filing follow-up.
aj: i'll kick off the canary in 5m and post results. tagging stakeholders: @kevin @ravi @sre-oncall
kevin: PR draft ready, pinging for review now :thumbsup:
maria: thanks team. once canary data in we'll decide revert vs patch. :shipit:
